blogs.title: Mining Math from the Web: How DeepSeekMath Built a 120 B‑Token Mathematical Corpus
blogs.description: Explore the data‑driven backbone of DeepSeekMath: the carefully engineered pipeline that extracts, filters, and annotates 120 B tokens of high‑quality mathematical content from Common Crawl. Learn how fastText classifiers, multi‑iteration refinement, and de‑duplication turned the web into a goldmine for mathematical reasoning.

blogs.title: Why Code First Yields Better Math: The Surprising Impact of Code Training on Mathematical Reasoning
blogs.description: Dive into the two‑stage vs one‑stage training experiments that show code pre‑training boosts both tool‑aided and pure reasoning abilities. Discover why starting from a code model like DeepSeek‑Coder enables 7 B LLMs to match closed‑source rivals on the toughest MATH benchmark.

blogs.title: From Rules to Models: The Evolution of Reward Signals in LLM Fine‑Tuning
blogs.description: Unpack the journey from rule‑based correctness checks to sophisticated neural reward models used in DeepSeekMath’s RL phase. Understand how each reward design influences policy updates and why “process” supervision (step‑by‑step rewards) matters for multi‑step reasoning.

blogs.title: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): A Memory‑Efficient RL Breakthrough for Math LLMs
blogs.description: Get an insider look at GRPO, a PPO variant that eliminates the critic model by leveraging group baselines. See how this lightweight algorithm gives a 5–10 % jump on GSM8K and MATH while cutting memory overhead, making RL feasible for 7 B models.

blogs.title: Unified RL Paradigm: Understanding SFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO in One Framework
blogs.description: Learn how different fine‑tuning methods—supervised, rejection sampling, direct preference optimization, policy gradient—fit into a single objective formula. The blog explains data source, reward function, and algorithmic differences that explain why GRPO outperforms other RL tricks.

blogs.title: Beyond Numbers: Where Does DeepSeekMath Still Fall Short?
blogs.description: A candid review of DeepSeekMath’s remaining challenges—geometry, theorem proving, few‑shot performance—and what implications this has for future research. The post also outlines concrete next steps proposed by the authors to push open source math LLMs closer to GPT‑4.
